configs.description: The PDU as it ships: the unit, two mounting brackets with their screws, a cord retainer and a power cord. Only the unit is drawn.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: The specification sheet 190174 p.4 prints "Weight" as 13.2 lb for the SP pair, with no word that says what it covers. The user manual I-00826 p.236 and p.238 print "Product Weight" as 6.84 lb (3.1 kg), one figure for every model. They print "Shipping Weight" as 9.92 and 10.58 lb. Both manual tables are headed with the non-SP models only. The manual's product weight is used for all four.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on the weight.

gaps.note: Every position is read off line drawings at a reduced scale and is good to about 2 mm. No dimensioned drawing of the faces is held.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing, or the 3D CAD zip once its terms allow.

gaps.note: User manual I-00826 p.19 says FEATURE is "Reserved for Future Use". Its pinout on p.256 marks DTR "Reserved". No document gives a media or a rate.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on the feature port once it has a use.

gaps.note: Searched: user manual I-00826 pp.18 to 19 and p.256, quick start I-00827 and specification sheet 190174. The p.19 table gives no row for EXPANSION. The p.256 pinout lists 12 V and RS-485 pins and names no media or rate.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on the expansion port.

gaps.note: The OLED display is drawn with the library's two-digit seven-segment part as a stand-in. That is not what the strip shows.
gaps.wanted: an OLED display part of the strip's size.

gaps.note: The specification sheet 190174 p.2 rear elevation shows a rectangular push-to-reset breaker about 14 by 16 mm. The library's push-to-reset part is round, and no rectangular part of that size exists.
The specification sheet 190174 p.2 gives 9 ft [2.75 m] for every model. The user manual I-00826 p.237 gives 10 ft (3 m) for the SP models.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on the SP cord.

gaps.note: The specification sheet 190174 p.4 prints "Full Load Input Current at V AC" as 15 A, and "Output Contentious Current" as 12 A. The user manual I-00826 p.236 prints "Maximum Peak Load" as 15 A and "Rated Load" as 12 A. The schema defines `input-current-a` as the derated rated current, so 12 A is stored. The sheet's p.2 table prints 15 A for the inlet and the breaker.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on what the sheet's full load input current means.

gaps.note: The specification sheet 190174 p.4 prints UL 60950-1 and CSA C22.2 No.60950-1, FCC Part 15, Class B. The user manual I-00826 p.237 prints UL 62368, UL 1283, UL 1449, FCC Class B, ICES 7 for the SP models. The sheet's list is used.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on the SP certifications.

gaps.note: The specification sheet 190174 p.2 shows two obround holes in each ear of its front and of its rear elevation. Each hole is 9.5 by 6.35 mm, four in each elevation. It shows two edge tabs in each elevation. The four mounting-ear holes on each of the front and rear are not drawn. The holes stand outside the 441 mm face, and decor there is never seen (L44). A part placed there is refused (L150). The schema line for `chassis.overhang` says: "Such a device draws its front at the rack-face width with the ears drawn". Two trials drew the front and rear 483 mm wide, the width the sheet prints over the ears. Each moved every part 21 mm to the right. Drawn as plain holes beyond the face, the holes drop the capability level from 4 to 2, because the face and body widths then disagree: "chassis width disagrees: front.w=483, rear.w=483, top.w=441, bottom.w=441, chassis.width=441". Lint passed, with L43 warnings that want a part seated within 25 mm of an end. Drawn as cutouts in the ears at the sheet's 483 mm width, the level stays 4. But the library lint adds many warnings for ports, lamps and buttons without cutouts: 27 new L39 warnings for each device, and over the four devices 108 of L39 and 8 of L53. The maintainer has left the ear holes undrawn, so the faces stay at the 441 mm body width. The tabs stand past the 44 mm height, which `overhang` does not cover.
gaps.wanted: Question for the maintainer: may a tab that stands past the 44 mm height be drawn?

gaps.note: The sheet p.2 front elevation prints a power symbol on the button and blue rating text above the outlet. The place of the logo is the region logo-zone. The user manual I-00826 p.15 rear photograph prints a ground symbol, an inlet legend and legends of the outlet block and breaker. The maintainer has left marks, colours and the rest to a later touch.
gaps.wanted: the maintainer's word on whether to draw printed marks.

capability.note: datasheet - specification sheet 190174 p.1 gives 8 individually controllable outlets, a web server, data logging and metering. So `outlet-switching` is true. Per-outlet metering is not stated.

chassis.note: datasheet - specification sheet 190174 p.2 prints 17.38 in [441] between the ear folds and 19.00 in [483] with the ears. It prints 1.74 in [44] high and 9.83 in [250] deep. Page 1 says phosphate pre-treated steel with a black powder coat. The colour #2c2e30 is the library's black. The p.1 photographs read nearer #2d3f42.

ears.note: estimated - the rack ears are the two mounting brackets of quick start I-00827 p.4, four screws each. The sheet's top view shows the flange at the front plane, so one flush position is stated. Each ear has two obround holes of 9.5 by 6.35 mm in the front and the rear elevation (specification sheet 190174 p.2). That is four in each view. The sheet prints 19.00 in [483] over the ears and 17.38 in [441] between the folds, so each ear reaches 21 mm. The holes are not drawn (gaps: ear-holes-and-tabs). The generic ear stands in.

end.note: estimated - the sheet shows two end views. Each has seven round holes, two near the rear, one at the middle and four on the front bracket plate. The upper one is turned a quarter turn, with the rear at its top and the device's bottom at its left. It is read as the left side, as a third-angle sheet places it beside the top view. The lower one, beside the rear elevation, is read as the right side. The scale is the printed 250 mm. A left view runs its depth from the rear and a right view from the front. A round head reads 6.5 mm. The left view also shows the inlet housing and the rear plate. The right view shows the bracket plate, the rear plate and four thin pieces. They are drawn as outlines.

front.note: estimated - specification sheet 190174 p.2 front elevation, counted twice at 800 and 1600 dpi. A blue-edged recess 375 by 40 mm holds 7 rows of staggered slots, 4.7 mm apart and about 15.9 mm along. The slot tile is the library's, so each slot is shorter than the sheet's. The illuminated power button is at the left. The touch strip holds the logo, numerals 1 to 8, two arrows and the OLED display. The ninth outlet stands in a dark surround at the right. The user manual I-00826 p.15 and p.17 show the same face. The blue marks read #34a0ee (4293 pixels of the sheet's front elevation).

input.note: datasheet - specification sheet 190174 p.2 table gives IEC C14, 15 A, 120 V, 60 Hz and a 9 ft [2.75 m] cord. The cord comes detachable with a retainer (quick start I-00827 p.4). The user manual I-00826 p.237 gives the SP models' cord as 10 ft, SignalSAFE IEC to NEMA 5-15P (gaps: cord-length). The input current states the 12 A rated load, as the schema defines it: derated. The sheet's p.4 "Full Load Input Current" prints 15 A (gaps: input-current).

left-out.note: not drawn: the cord retainer clip stands below the 44 mm body (specification sheet 190174 p.2, front, rear and end views). Only its two screws are drawn. The wire loop in the top and end views stands up to 13.6 mm behind the view's rear edge, beyond the printed 250 mm depth. The schema line for `chassis.overhang` says: "`left` and `right` are as seen from the front." It has no key above or below the face. Not drawn: the edge tabs, which stand outside the 44 mm body. The front elevation shows one above about 54 mm from the left and one below about 314 mm from the left. The rear elevation shows one above at the port block and one below under outlet 2. Not drawn: the ear holes, two in each ear of both elevations, which stand outside the 441 mm face (gaps: ear-holes-and-tabs). Not drawn: the fine pieces at the rear edge of the top and end views, 0.2 to 3.5 mm, under 1.3 pt on the sheet. Not drawn: the printed marks. The maintainer has left marks, colours and the rest to a later touch. The sheet's front elevation prints the logo on the touch strip. It is 153 by 52 px at 1600 dpi and 76 by 27 px at 800 dpi. Its place is the region logo-zone, which reserves the box and draws no mark. The power symbol on the button is 69 by 64 px at 1600 dpi. The blue rating text above the front outlet is 153 by 24 px at 800 dpi. The user manual I-00826 p.15 rear photograph is 911 by 83 px. It prints the ground symbol beside the stud, about 11 by 14 px. It prints the inlet legend with capitals about 5 px tall. It prints the legends of the outlet block and breaker with capitals about 3 px tall. The sheet's rear elevation prints none of those three.

method.note: Searched: specification sheet 190174, 5 pages, all looked at at 150 dpi. Also searched: user manual I-00826, pages 15 to 20 and 234 to 238, and quick start I-00827, all 8 printed pages. The size is printed. Every position inside it is read off the p.2 elevations at the scale of the printed 441 mm body. Each is good to about 2 mm. The maker's 3D CAD zip is not opened.

other-sides.note: estimated - the bottom is built from the sheet's top view, as no document shows this side. A bottom view mirrors left and right, so its outlines are turned across. The four screw heads repeat the top view's, as their pattern is symmetric to within 1 mm. The square stands at the lower edge tab of the front elevation, about 314 mm from the left.

outlets.note: datasheet - user manual I-00826 p.234 and p.236 give 9 outlets in total, 8 controlled, type NEMA 5-15R. Each is std/nema-5-15r@1. The outlet rating is 12 A and the breaker 15 A (specification sheet 190174 p.2 table).

port-legends.note: estimated - the port legends are read off the user manual I-00826 p.19 photograph. It is 720 by 241 pixels, about 4.5 px per mm. Its capitals are about 11 pixels tall, so each legend is placed to about 2 mm.

rear.note: estimated - specification sheet 190174 p.2 rear elevation and user manual I-00826 pp.15, 19 and 20. From the left stand the inlet, the breaker, the ground stud and eight outlets on a 27.9 mm pitch. Each outlet has a lamp under it and a numeral 1 to 8. Then come the reset hole, two Ethernet jacks, two USB-A, one USB-B and four more RJ45 jacks. Four round marks sit at the corners of that port block, and one dark window below the reset hole. The manual p.19 says the yellow LED of ETH2 has no function, and the window is drawn dark. The two crossed screws either side of the inlet sit where the cord retainer's holes are (quick start I-00827 p.5, figure D). The sheet's screws read about 7 mm and the library's head is 3.6 mm. The sheet's lamps are rectangles 3.5 by 2.5 mm, so they use the library's rectangular lamp. The lit green lamp reads #1fde2e (365 pixels of the user manual I-00826 p.20 photograph). No held picture shows a lit red lamp.

top.note: estimated - the sheet's top view shows four round screw heads and one square at the front left. That square is the upper edge tab seen from above. The scale is the printed 441 mm. A round head reads 6.5 mm and the square 8 mm. The depth axis runs from the rear, so y 0 is the rear edge of the printed 250 mm. The view also shows the eight outlet tops, three outlines of the breaker and inlet, and the front flange. They are drawn as outlines, placed from the four screw heads.
